display.title: Episode 141: The Island of Treasures (Month of Elul)
display.summary_short: A shipwrecked man is crowned king of an island and spends its whole treasury there, never guessing he must one day leave: a parable about this world and the next, told in Elul.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi reports that big drawings are pouring in for the Shofar Gadol contest and reminds listeners that in Elul Hashem is like a King in the field, close and joyful. After the Hakochainik march and a sponsor message, twin brothers lead the Shema. Story time, a few weeks before Rosh Hashanah, is a parable: a lone survivor of a shipwreck drifts to a strange island, where the people crown him king and hand him the keys to the royal treasury. He spends every coin beautifying the island, until a servant brings back his old rags and reveals the island's secret: each king rules only until the next castaway arrives. He leaves as poor as he came, wishing he had sent shiploads of treasure home. Uncle Yossi explains that the island is this world, the treasures are mitzvos, and the Torah is the key, as the Mishnah teaches that this world is a corridor to the World to Come. In Elul we gather mitzvos through teshuvah, tefillah and tzedakah. The show closes with news of a surprise guest next week and a reminder about the contest.
display.lesson: This world is only a corridor to the World to Come: use your time here to send ahead treasures of Torah and mitzvos.
